claims.text: Ab initio calculations combined with machine-learning potentials can be used to tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Ab initio calculations combined with machine-learning potentials can be used to tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The proposed computational method is applicable to low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications.
The initial material class comprises non-equiatomic HEAs with varying compositions.
Ab initio calculations with machine-learning potentials can predict magnetic behavior in these HEAs.
Ab initio calculations with machine-learning potentials can predict magnetocaloric behavior in these HEAs.
The proposed computational approach can optimize HEA compositions for magnetic and magnetocaloric performance.
HEA microstructure and composition mediate magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
Combining ab initio calculations with machine-learning potentials enables prediction of magnetic transitions.
Predicting magnetic transitions and magnetocaloric behavior enables identification of optimal HEA compositions for specific applications.
Computationally optimized non-equiatomic HEAs will have improved magnetic behavior.
Computationally optimized non-equiatomic HEAs will have improved magnetocaloric behavior.
Computational optimization may increase cooling efficiency.
Computational optimization may increase the useful temperature range.
Current computational methods and experimental techniques impose limitations on the proposed approach.
